title: QSAR machine learning finds ionic liquid inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 main protease
summary: Multitask machine learning QSAR models were trained on 2844 compounds with EC50 and IC50 data and validated by cross-validation and external test sets. Thirteen compounds predicted to have high anti-Mpro activity were tested in a fluorescence assay, and the six most active were counter-screened with trypsin and papain; the best inhibition was in the tens of micromolar range.
organization: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine; Institute of Bioorganic Chemistry and Petrochemistry V.P. Kukhar

evidence.tested: In vitro fluorescence protease assay of 13 predicted compounds with counter-screening, plus external test sets for the models.
evidence.unknown: Potency is weak; only a small set of compounds tested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning predicted Mpro activity to prioritize compounds for testing.
